predecessors.note: 'The Lutici were first recorded by written sources in the context of the uprising of 983'; they were 'at least in part' a continuation of the Veleti. The land had been tributary to the Saxon duke under the Billung March since 936.

predecessors.note: The Billung March of Hermann Billung 'was finally abandoned following the uprising of the Obotrites and Veleti' in 983 (Billung March page); the Liutizi and Hevelli lands lay mostly in the neighbouring Marca Geronis.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Lutici row; its Kingdom of Germany and Holy Roman Empire shapes draw the Elbe-Oder land as imperial from 947 or 961, so this region overlaps them). The page fixes the federation 'between the Warnow and Mildenitz in the west, the Havel in the south and the Oder in the east' and does not give the Elbe or the Peene; a six-point polygon follows those rivers, about 23,800 km2. The infobox gives no area. The page also says the federation 'disintegrated in a civil war' in 1056/1057 and that Henry of the Obotrites subdued all Lutician areas north of the Havel in 1093, so the polygon is the federation's nominal extent, with real control varying: the contest events 1093-1128 mark the Obotrite and Saxon pressure.

region.text: 'between the Warnow and Mildenitz in the west, the Havel in the south and the Oder in the east': the Redarii, Tollensians, Kessinians and Circipanians

ledger.note: 983: the Slav rising founds the Lutician federation. 'The Lutici were first recorded by written sources in the context of the uprising of 983'; Otto III was crowned king at Aachen at Christmas 983 during the uprising. The Redarii are mentioned from 928 and the Tollensians and Circipanians from 955.

region.text: Brandenburg an der Havel and its Havel country

ledger.note: 991: the Havel country at Brandenburg is fought over. The page: 'Brandenburg is temporarily reconquered, then besieged' in 991-993; the Saxon army was victorious in 993. Brandenburg's holder in 991 is not named.

region.text: Brandenburg an der Havel and its Havel country

ledger.note: 993: the Saxon army is victorious at Brandenburg. The Lutici allied with the emperor against Bolesław I of Poland on 28 March 1003 at Quedlinburg and broke with him in 1017; after the sack of Werben in 1035 a Saxon-led campaign forced them to accept tribute and hostages.

region.text: 'between the Warnow and Mildenitz in the west, the Havel in the south and the Oder in the east': the Redarii, Tollensians, Kessinians and Circipanians

ledger.note: 1093: Henry of the Obotrites subdues the Lutician areas north of the Havel. 'Henry subdues all Lutician areas north of the Havel after an Obodrite revolt'; he consolidated the Obodrite realm in 1090. Revolts followed in 1100/1101 and 1110; in 1114 Lothair subdued prince Dumar of the Kessini and again attacked them in 1121.

region.text: 'between the Warnow and Mildenitz in the west, the Havel in the south and the Oder in the east': the Redarii, Tollensians, Kessinians and Circipanians

ledger.note: 1128: the Lutician primores convert to Christianity and the contest closes. 'the Lutician primores of this area converted to Christianity in 1128'; Lothair destroyed a Lutician civitas and temple, probably Radgosc, in 1126/1127; Otto of Bamberg destroyed temples at Wolgast and Gützkow. The end year is the page's last dated step; real control had passed to Obotrite, Saxon and Pomeranian princes by then.

region.text: 'between the Warnow and Mildenitz in the west, the Havel in the south and the Oder in the east': the Redarii, Tollensians, Kessinians and Circipanians

ledger.note: 1157: the Margraviate of Brandenburg is the successor. The infobox lists the Margraviate of Brandenburg from 1157; the body text describes no conquest in that year, but says the territory was partitioned among the Obodrite principalities and Mecklenburg in the west, the re-constituted Northern March (Brandenburg) in the south and Pomerania in the east, in the first half of the 12th century. Lothair gave the Northern March to Albert the Bear in 1134. The Wendish Crusade of 1147 targeted the Obodrite and Lutician areas.

region.text: 'between the Warnow and Mildenitz in the west, the Havel in the south and the Oder in the east': the Redarii, Tollensians, Kessinians and Circipanians

ledger.note: 1157: the Lutician lands are shared out. Infobox: 'collapse' in the 12th century and the Margraviate of Brandenburg from 1157; the Lutici were assimilated by German settlers during the Ostsiedlung in the 13th century.

wars.outcome: The rising of the Obotrites and Veleti ended the Billung March and the German hold east of the Elbe; the Lutici appear in the written sources in this context.

wars.name: German-Polish War (1002-1018)
wars.outcome: The Lutici entered an alliance with the emperor against Bolesław I of Poland on 28 March 1003; the Peace of Bautzen of 1018 ended the war and the Lutici attacked the Obodrites in the same year.

notes: One page opened (budget 2-5; the page is long and dated). The Lutici page has no area; the polygon is the researcher's reading of its river description. The end year 1157 follows the infobox's Margraviate of Brandenburg date and eu-08-b's Holy Roman Empire ledger (gain from Lutici 1157); the page itself dates the federation's disintegration 1056/57, Obotrite domination 1093, Lothair's destruction of Radgosc 1126/27 and the partition 'in the first half of the 12th century'. The Hevelli (Brandenburg an der Havel, Havelberg) are an associate tribe, not core, and are drawn only as the 991-993 contest circle; a Hevelli dossier is optional (eu-08-a). Gazetteer lacks Brandenburg an der Havel, Havelberg and Rethra/Radgosc (coordinates used). Whether the Lutici were an empire tributary after 1035 is not drawn (no vassal event in a vassal's own ledger).
